text: Sources: Ofcom, Media Nations 2025 and Audio Listening 2025. Demand for gestures remains a hypothesis.

25 seconds
Our first user is a student with a Mac, a smart lamp and Spotify. Adjusting the room still means reaching for an app, finding a switch or speaking a command. The cost we want to reduce is that interruption. Ofcom found smart speakers in 40% of UK households, and three in five smart-speaker users said a request for a radio station had played the wrong thing. That is evidence of control friction, not proof that they will pay for gestures.

Sources and qualifications
https://www.ofcom.org.uk/siteassets/resources/documents/research-and-data/multi-sector/media-nations/2025/media-nations-2025-uk-report.pdf (printed page 92, Q1 2025 smart-speaker ownership)
https://www.ofcom.org.uk/tv-radio-and-on-demand/digital-radio/top-trends-uk-listening-habits-2025 (21 May 2025, wrong radio-station playback). Do not interpret this as 60% of requests failing.

text: Current scope: macOS, webcam, calibrated targets, paired Zigbee lamp and the Spotify desktop app.

20 seconds
Spellcast uses the webcam already on the Mac. We calibrate where the lamp and speaker appear in the camera view. Pointing selects the device, and the other hand controls it. The current code connects the lamp through Zigbee2MQTT and controls the Mac Spotify app. It also includes Calm, Study and Party scenes. This prototype uses two-dimensional camera calibration, not automatic room understanding.

Sources and qualifications

text: Webcam perception runs on the Mac. Lamp control needs the local Zigbee setup. Spotify remains its own service.

45 seconds. Switch to the running app.
Before pitching, pair the bulb, open and sign into Spotify, permit Automation, enable the camera and calibrate both target boxes. Start with no scene active.
0-15 sec: point at the lamp. Use the other hand open for ON, fist for OFF, then reopen and move it up or down for brightness.
15-30 sec: point directly at the speaker. Move the other hand to adjust Spotify volume.
30-45 sec: touch the two index fingertips together twice, separating them between contacts, to enter Calm. Repeat if time permits to show Study. Keep Party optional. Scene presets override individual lamp gestures.
Say: One camera, two devices, and a room that responds to where you point.
If hardware fails, use the on-screen controls to explain the same interaction and say clearly which connection is unavailable. Do not imply a recorded result.

Sources and qualifications
Gesture evidence: src/control/useTwoHandLampControl.ts, useSpotifyHandControl.ts, useTwoHandSceneControl.ts. Current scene sequence: none, Calm, Study, Party, none.

20 seconds
Apps give precise controls. Voice can work across the room. Flic already sells physical controls with gesture support. Spellcast adds a different selection method: point at the actual visible object. We are not claiming that gesture control is new, or that this prototype is universally easier. The hypothesis is that direct pointing is useful in a quiet desk setup.

name: TAM is a broad proxy. SAM, SOM and £29/year are pl
text: TAM is a broad proxy. SAM, SOM and £29/year are planning assumptions. Sources: ONS and Ofcom, 2025 data.

20 seconds
Our first audience is students with compatible desk setups. For scale, we use a broad UK smart-speaker household proxy, not a count of compatible Spellcast buyers. Twenty-nine million UK households times 40% gives 11.6 million. Our serviceable scenario assumes just 1% also meets the Mac, webcam, lighting and willingness criteria. Our first-year target is 1,000 paying rooms. We must measure that 1% assumption and demand before relying on this market case.

Sources and qualifications
https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/birthsdeathsandmarriages/families/bulletins/familiesandhouseholds/2025 (2025 household estimate, released 17 April 2026)
https://www.ofcom.org.uk/siteassets/resources/documents/research-and-data/multi-sector/media-nations/2025/media-nations-2025-uk-report.pdf (Q1 2025 ownership share)
Calculation: 29,000,000 × 0.40 = 11,600,000. SAM scenario: 11,600,000 × 0.01 = 116,000. SOM target: 1,000 / 116,000 = 0.86%. Price proposal: GBP 29 per year.

text: Target funnel: 400 qualified visits × 25% activation = 100 users. Proposed channels and conversion, not traction.

15 seconds
We start in Durham with students who already own compatible hardware. Recruit 20 supervised testers through computing and gaming societies. Then share a real demonstration and a compatibility guide with maker communities and desk-setup creators. The planning funnel is 400 qualified visits and 25% activation to reach 100 installed setups. These are targets, not existing users.

Sources and qualifications
Acquisition proposal. No university, society, creator partnership or installed-user count has been verified. Activation means a user completes a gesture command on a real paired device.

text: Pricing hypothesis. Hardware and music service costs are separate. No cloud video inference is required.

15 seconds
The beta is free. Our paid-launch proposal is 29 pounds per year for one supported room. Enthusiasts would pay for a maintained control layer and compatibility updates. Existing hardware is separate. At 1,000 customers this is 29,000 pounds in annual gross revenue before fees, tax and support. We will test payment after users have tried it. Willingness to pay and renewal are unproven.

Sources and qualifications
Commercial proposal, not an existing subscription. No revenue or customer commitments have been verified. Hardware, Spotify service and integration support costs remain separate.

TAM proxy combines two UK datasets for 2025 with slightly different measurement periods. It does not measure ownership of a supported lamp, a Mac, or demand for a webcam interface. text: Proposed go / no-go thresholds. Compare with current controls and measure camera comfort, fatigue and setup friction.

Q&A
Run a pilot with 20 students who have the supported setup. Compare the same lamp and music tasks using Spellcast and their existing controls, counterbalancing the order. Count completed actions and unintended activations. Test daylight and dim rooms. Follow up after one week and offer a real paid reservation only after a trial. These thresholds are proposed decision rules, not results.

Sources and qualifications
Research design proposal. No customer interviews, usability study, retention test or willingness-to-pay evidence was supplied or conducted for this deck.
